question: Can a knowledge retriever be pre-trained without supervision, using masked language modelling as the signal, so that a language model retrieves and attends over a large corpus?
hypothesis: A retrieval that improves the language model's perplexity should be rewarded, so MLM pre-training can teach the retriever useful retrieval and improve Open-QA over implicit-knowledge and heuristic-retrieval systems.
contributions: First unsupervised pre-training of a knowledge retriever with MLM, backpropagating through a retrieval step over millions of documents
Asynchronous MIPS index refresh to make this tractable
New state of the art on three Open-QA benchmarks by 4-16% absolute accuracy, with interpretability and modularity

method.summary: A latent-variable model p(y|x)=sum_z p(y|z,x)p(z|x): a BERT-style dense retriever (inner product, MIPS top-k) feeds a BERT knowledge-augmented encoder. Pre-trained with salient-span MLM on Wikipedia or CC-News while the MIPS index is refreshed asynchronously, then fine-tuned on Open-QA with the document index fixed.
method.task: retrieval-augmented MLM pre-training; open-domain QA fine-tuning

datasets.name: Wikipedia (20 Dec 2018 snapshot) as knowledge corpus Z and pre-training corpus X
datasets.preprocessing: greedily split into chunks of up to 288 BERT wordpieces

datasets.name: CC-News (pre-training corpus X option 2)
datasets.source: authors' reproduction of the corpus of Liu et al. (2019)

datasets.name: NaturalQuestions-Open
datasets.split: train/test as in Lee et al. 2019; dev used for ablations
datasets.preprocessing: only questions with short answer type of at most five tokens; suggested Wikipedia document not given to model

models.name: REALM
models.architecture: BERT-style dense retriever (Embed_input, Embed_doc with linear projections) plus BERT knowledge-augmented encoder
models.init_from: retriever warm-started with Inverse Cloze Task (Lee et al. 2019); encoder from uncased BERT-base

other.retriever_layers_hidden_heads: inferred: BERT-base style, not stated for the retriever

training.objective: maximise log p(y|x) with top-k approximated marginalisation; MLM loss at pre-training, span-match likelihood at fine-tuning
training.hardware: 64 Google Cloud TPUs for pre-training; MIPS document embedding parallelised over 16 TPUs

other.salient_span_masking: BERT tagger on CoNLL-2003 for named entities plus regex for dates; one span masked per sentence
other.trivial_retrieval: exclude the document the masked sentence came from when X=Z
other.finetune_hparams: reused from Lee et al. (2019); index built once and Embed_doc not updated, Embed_input still fine-tuned
other.finetune_hardware: entire model can run on a single machine with a 12GB GPU

inference.decoding: answer span extraction from retrieved documents
inference.retrieval: MIPS over about 13M chunks; top-5 candidates at fine-tuning inference; 8 (with null) during pre-training

metrics.name: Exact match
metrics.definition: predicted answer string matches any reference answer (regex for CuratedTrec)

metrics.name: Zero-shot retrieval Recall@5
metrics.definition: how often the gold answer appears in top-5 retrievals before fine-tuning

eval.protocol: test-set exact match for main results; NQ dev for ablations; single numbers, no seeds or significance tests stated

limits: Index refresh was used only in pre-training; fine-tuning builds the MIPS index once and does not update Embed_doc, and the authors say refreshing might further help (footnote 3).
T5 baselines come from concurrent work with an improved fine-tuning procedure; T5 saw SQuAD data in pre-training, REALM did not.
T5 not evaluated on CuratedTrec because answers are regexes.
Even with an explicit retriever the encoder still memorises some knowledge (Appendix C, 'Thatcher' example).
Called the minimal instantiation; structured, multilingual and multi-modal extensions left to future work.
No seeds, variance or compute cost in time stated.

code.snippet: p(y | x) = sum_{z in Z} p(y | z, x) p(z | x)
grad log p(y|x) = sum_z r(z) grad f(x,z), r(z) = (p(y|z,x)/p(y|x) - 1) p(z|x)
